title: Tenant isolation
description: Multi-tenant data isolation for SaaS apps: resolve the tenant from the verified session and membership (client-sent ids are only selectors), PostgreSQL row-level security with transaction-local tenant settings and a non-bypass role, a tenant-scoped repository, and a reusable cross-tenant test kit.

notes: Requires a TypeScript build and the WHATWG URL and Fetch Request/Response APIs: Node.js 22+, Bun, Deno, Cloudflare Workers, Next.js route handlers and Hono.
Database enforcement requires PostgreSQL 9.5+ (row-level security); the resolver and scoped repository work with any $1-placeholder executor, but other databases need their own enforcement.
No runtime packages, environment reads, timers or network activity at install or import time.

configuration: Apply schema.sql (or appRoleSql() and tenantTableSql('your_table') for each tenant table) as the database owner; every tenant table needs a tenant_id column leading its indexes.
Run application queries as a role that is neither superuser nor BYPASSRLS: log in as a member of app_user, or pass { role: 'app_user' } to withTenant and GRANT app_user to the login user.
Supply session(request) from your verified session or token and memberships(userId) from your membership table; optionally a selector (headerSelector, pathSelector or subdomainSelector).
On a connection pool, give the executor a transaction(work) that checks out one client for BEGIN ... COMMIT so set_config and SET LOCAL ROLE stay on that connection.
Call assertTenantIsolation from your own test suite against each tenant table in a test database.
limitations: Database enforcement is PostgreSQL row-level security only; MySQL, SQLite and document stores rely on the scoped repository alone, which is application-level filtering.
Superusers, BYPASSRLS roles and connections that skip withTenant's SET LOCAL ROLE bypass every policy; inspectIsolation and the test kit detect a bypassing role but cannot stop an app from using one.

inspectIsolation checks that every permissive policy references the tenant setting textually; it does not prove the expression is correct (for example `... OR true`), which only the test kit's behavior checks show.
The test kit's setting-lifetime check needs a dedicated connection (`client`); with only a pool it reports not-checked.

Tested on PostgreSQL semantics through PGlite 0.5.8, a single connection running as a superuser with SET LOCAL ROLE to a NOLOGIN role; pooled multi-connection behavior, LOGIN roles, PgBouncer transaction pooling and hosted Postgres were not exercised.
The BEGIN/COMMIT fallback in withTenant is only correct on a dedicated client; on a pool the executor must supply transaction().

Policies cover tables generated with tenantTableSql or schema.sql; views (unless security_invoker), SECURITY DEFINER functions, foreign keys into shared tables, sequences, large objects and storage buckets need their own review.
The scoped repository handles single-table get/list/insert/update/delete by id; joins and raw SQL must add the tenant predicate themselves (RLS still applies to them).
Tenant resolution trusts whatever session(request) and memberships(userId) return; session security, membership administration and tenant provisioning remain project responsibilities.
decisions: PostgreSQL RLS via transaction-local set_config('app.tenant_id'); tables get FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY
a tenant the user is not a member of → 404 not-found by default (hiddenStatus: 403 to change)
several memberships and no selector → 400 tenant-required; none → 403 no-tenant
tenant ids 1-128 chars of [A-Za-z0-9_.:-]; memberships are read on every request

verification.command: npm run build && node --test tests/tenant-isolation.test.mjs tests/tenant-isolation-sql.test.mjs
behaviors: a client-sent tenant id (header, path or subdomain) is honored only when it matches a membership of the verified session user; otherwise not-a-member (404 by default, 403 optional)
requests without a valid session are refused with 401 whatever tenant they name
malformed tenant selectors are refused before any lookup; a selector cannot override a verified session tenant claim
with no selector a single membership decides, several need a choice (400) and none is refused (403)
memberships are read on every request, so a revoked membership is refused at once
every scoped statement carries tenant_id = $n, and another tenant's id returns null, false or not-found
scoped inserts force the tenant column and refuse another tenant's value; updates cannot change the tenant or id columns; column names come only from an allowlist
withTenant runs set_config(app.tenant_id, id, true) and optional SET LOCAL ROLE inside one transaction and rolls back on error
generated SQL enables and forces RLS with one USING and WITH CHECK predicate that matches no row when the tenant is unset
on PostgreSQL as app_user an unscoped SELECT returns only the current tenant's rows
on PostgreSQL UPDATE and DELETE of another tenant's id affect 0 rows, and INSERT or UPDATE into another tenant fails the WITH CHECK policy
on PostgreSQL no tenant set returns 0 rows and the tenant setting and role do not outlive the transaction
the scoped repository still filters by tenant on a connection that bypasses RLS

inspectIsolation reports missing FORCE, roles that bypass RLS and permissive policies whose USING or WITH CHECK does not read the tenant setting (policies are OR-ed), matching the table's schema (default public)
assertTenantIsolation passes all 9 checks on RLS tables and reports each leak on an unprotected table, cleaning up its seeded rows
the test kit checks the tenant setting before and after commit on one dedicated client, fails a session-level (leaking) setting, and reports not-checked instead of passed when given only a pool
through the Fetch handler a user of tenant A gets 404 for tenant B's rows on read and delete, and B's row is unchanged

changes: inspectIsolation flags permissive policies that do not read the tenant setting and matches pg_policies and pg_class by schema (new options { schema, setting }).
Test kit checks carry a status; the setting-lifetime check runs on one dedicated client (new client option) and is not-checked on a pool instead of passing trivially.
First release: trusted tenant resolution and Fetch handler, PostgreSQL row-level security helpers and schema, scoped repository, isolation self-check and cross-tenant test kit.
